text:
oncall-bot: PAGER: gpu-prod-us-west-2 pool at 100% allocation and request queue growing. HPA not scaling. Severity: P2. Paging #incidents and #eng-sre.

alex: seeing large queue growth for inference requests, error rate up ~12% over last 10m, p95 latency spiked. Grafana shows pod count stable; HPA target metrics missing.

maya: checking metrics pipeline — prometheus->adapter lag seems high. Running `kubectl get --namespace kube-system pods` shows `metrics-adapter` restarting a few times.

diego: can you paste adapter logs? tagging @infra-sre for help with node pool limits and quotas.

infra-sre: looking now — no cloud quota error in console, but node group hit autoscaling cooldown and k8s HPA didn't get custom metrics. Could be adapter backlog.

alex: adapter logs (last 100 lines):
```
I0322 14:02:10.123 adapter.go:215] processing metrics request for hpa/default/llm-inference
E0322 14:02:12.789 queue.go:88] failed to process metric: context deadline exceeded
W0322 14:02:13.456 prometheus.go:98] scrape backlog: 2300 samples pending
E0322 14:02:14.001 auth.go:45] token refresh failed: response 401
```

maya: auth failures around token refresh — kube-service-account token was rotated 15m ago by automation. adapter started returning 401s to Prometheus remote read, which created backlog. HPA queries rely on adapter; with backlog the HPA controller sees stale values (0) and won't scale.

eng-runtime: confirming: HPA is configured to use custom metric `inference_queue_length` via custom.metrics.k8s.io. When adapter returns 500/401, custom metrics API returns empty and HPA stays put.

ops-lead: impact? which customers affected?

customer-success-bot: active sessions: 17 enterprise customers in us-west-2 experiencing increased latency and throttled requests; 3 reported degraded service by webhooks. No full data loss, but user-facing errors on heavy batch jobs.

alex: mitigation plan: 1) short-term: manually add capacity to GPU pool (create 2 extra g4dn nodes) and scale inference deployment replicas up to absorb queue; 2) fix metrics-adapter auth (reapply service account secret), restart adapter; 3) re-enable HPA after metrics backlog drains and confirm autoscaler resumes.

diego: manual scale command I'm going to run now (GCP example):
```
gcloud compute instance-groups managed resize gpu-prod-group --region us-west2 --size=12
kubectl scale deployment llm-inference -n prod --replicas=20
```

infra-sre: before we add nodes, double-checking there aren't rate limits on driver provisioning. If cloud quota is OK we'll create nodes; if not we should reroute some traffic to hosts in eu-west-1 as temporary fallback.

maya: meanwhile, for metrics-adapter fix: reapply secret and restart pods:
```
kubectl -n kube-system delete secret prometheus-adapter-sa-token
kubectl -n kube-system apply -f /infra/k8s/prometheus-adapter-sa.yaml
kubectl -n kube-system rollout restart deployment prometheus-adapter
```

alex: performing controlled restart of adapter now. Will monitor custom.metrics.k8s.io endpoint.

eng-runtime: note — while adapter backlog is clearing, HPA might read zeros for a minute. We should temporarily force HPA minReplicas higher so we don't drop below critical capacity.

ops-lead: set minReplicas to 8 in HPA for llm-inference. Make it an emergency patch and annotate for rollback.

alex: patched HPA: `kubectl patch hpa llm-inference -n prod -p '{"spec":{"minReplicas":8}}'` — confirmed new min.

oncall-bot: Incident timeline updated. Severity remains P2. Paging suppressed to on-call rotation for next 30m.

infra-sre: cloud console shows instance group resize accepted; provisioning new nodes now. ETA ~6m.

maya: prometheus-adapter logs after restart:
```
I0322 14:09:05.012 adapter.go:110] authorized with service account
I0322 14:09:05.523 queue.go:45] drained backlog: 2300 -> 1200
I0322 14:10:12.231 queue.go:45] drained backlog: 1200 -> 200
I0322 14:11:40.987 prometheus.go:75] custom metric inference_queue_length now returning 420
```

eng-runtime: HPA observed value now non-zero and started scaling activities. K8s is creating new pods; some will attach to existing GPUs.

diego: replica scale completed, new pods becoming ready. Queue length decreasing.

customer-success-bot: CS alerted enterprise contacts for 3 impacted customers with ETA and mitigation steps. No escalations requested.

ops-lead: good. After nodes are healthy and autoscaler resumes, we should revert emergency HPA minReplicas and annotate incident.

alex: new metrics: queue length down from 4800 -> 600 over 12m, error rate down to 1.8%. p95 latency normalizing.

infra-sre: nodes provisioned and in Ready state. Autoscaler back to normal. K8s HPA reports desired replicas 14 -> 10 as load drops.

maya: recommend follow-ups: 1) add test for service account token rotation to catch adapter auth regression in staging; 2) add alert for prometheus-adapter queue depth > 500; 3) document emergency HPA minReplicas runbook.

ops-lead: agreed. Assigning action items: @maya write runbook, @infra-sre implement adapter queue alert, @eng-runtime add token rotation test to CI.

alex: handing off to @maya for post-incident analysis and RCA. On-call clear for now, but keep channel open for 30m.

maya: taking over for RCA. Initial root cause candidate: service-account token rotation without updating adapter secret -> adapter auth 401 -> metrics backlog -> HPA reads stale/empty -> autoscaler didn't add nodes -> GPU pool exhausted -> request queue growth + throttling. Will validate and produce timeline.

oncall-bot: oncall handoff: @alex -> @maya. Next oncall: @diego.

end of thread.
